# Reading recording packs for useful gameplay feedback

Sol 6.1 / xhigh research · 2026-10-23 (coordinator history extends into October 24 UTC)

**Recommendation:** use the pack to answer a few player questions, with the owner's notes first in importance, then inspect evidence around those questions. Keep technical validity checks short. A technically clean recording is evidence that a particular run worked; it is not evidence that the game is enjoyable. The largest immediate gains are better selection and interpretation, followed by joining the existing play-timeline analysis into the pack. A new analytics platform would add little.

This is research for the Opus assessment and coordinator consolidation, not feature acceptance or a change to owner policy. In particular, retain the independent Sol gate, coordinator inspection, stage-exit Opus experience audit, once-per-wave taste/stewardship reviews and canonical merge gate.

## What a pack contains today

Signal below means usefulness for **gameplay/quality decisions**, not how much engineering work an artifact required. [R1–R4]

| Artifact | Signal | Useful evidence and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `summary.json` | High for triage; low for experience | Tiny technical verdict, failures/unproven checks, frame gaps/work/recorder cost, memory, errors, draws, hardware/build and attention count. **No pacing, friction or feedback-note summary.** A pass cannot answer whether a discovery chain is clear. |
| `story.md` | High | Checks, timestamped attention entries with strip links, activity shares, progression gaps, region droughts and filtered event timeline. Best current entry point. Attention is chronological, not ranked by player consequence. Much of its length is repeated hitch detail. |
| Root play timeline + `analyseTimeline` report | High, when supplied | Existing authoritative model of new things by kind, 20-minute discovery gaps including start/end, >90-second empty travel by craft, idle/background waiting, gathers, deaths/recovery and time/location-stamped notes. Handles rotated chunks. **A standalone timeline export/report is not in these packs.** Some timeline events are embedded in flight events; that is not automatically a complete session export. |
| Attention strips | High for a specific incident; medium by default | Default ±2 seconds at 12 fps: about 48 frames in a 1280-pixel-wide sheet, roughly 155×87 scene pixels per tile. Good for collision, gross motion/pop-in and before/after changes; poor for HUD text, subtle warning visibility or long confusion. Labels add time/tick/depth/speed, not player intent. |
| Three `R*` unflagged strips | Medium | Cheap defense against an attention system that misses visual failures. Deterministic pseudo-random selection avoids flagged moments, but is not representative coverage of activities/regions. Read one relevant control, not automatically all three. |
| `contact-sheet.jpg` | Medium for taste; low for friction | Event snapshots give a visual overview. Event selection and tiny tiles conceal slow failures and UI details. The fixed-view sheet is a separate once-per-wave taste tool. |
| Three charts | Medium on a flag | Frame-time, memory and activity shape can identify sustained trouble or timing clusters. Numbers usually suffice first. A short streaming-in memory rise is not a leak; current code requires duration/coverage before judging flatness. |
| `timeline.html` | High as a human navigation aid; low as model input | Synchronizes video, frame-time/memory charts and events. Seek to a question. Never paste its HTML into model context: some examples inline megabytes of video. It is not an extra independent source of truth. |
| Video | High for selected sequences | 12 fps, up to 1280×720, with page-clock alignment. Driver/CDP video includes the page/HUD; **owner-playtest video and event snapshots capture the WebGL canvas, omitting DOM HUD, menus and feedback UI. Both video paths are silent.** Neither proves the audible mix, and 12 fps does not measure 60 fps smoothness. Latest code segments playtest video and records retention/loss. |
| Fixed views + `report.md/json` + changed-view triptychs | High for regression; medium for taste; low for pacing | Per-machine baselines and SSIM detect visual changes. A change is not necessarily a regression, and similarity is not an art-quality score. Current documented coverage is **143 captured, 18 quarantined, 125 eligible**, plus pending views. Diver-only, fixed-time views miss cockpit/UI and many encounter states. Quarantined views remain useful pictures but supply no regression pass. |
| `analysis.json` | Medium, targeted | Structured source for story/attention/pacing; useful for querying a flagged episode. Reading it in full after the story duplicates much of the same information. |
| `recording/header.json`, NDJSON, `run.json`, `probe.json` | High for diagnosis; low by default | Header identifies recording source, clocks, settings, coverage and loss. Frame rows have component timings; 4 Hz samples have position, vitals, craft charge/health and renderer state; events include commands/refusals, damage, threats, saves, notes and milestones. Driver-only system sampling adds RSS/GPU data. Raw rows are for bounded queries, not an LLM reading millions of numbers. |

Important missing or weak questions:

- **Pacing:** no per-minute new-thing curve, time to first useful interaction/tool/expedition, recipe-trip workload or purposeful/empty backtracking report. Current REC pacing is a motion/action heuristic: “doing” lasts three seconds after an action/refusal/milestone. A held gather or thoughtful stationary observation can be misclassified. Frequent refusals can increase “doing.” The latest code excludes waiting/menus from its play clock, but it still differs from the simulation timeline. Use the simulation model for progression; wall time still matters for frustration.
- **Friction:** raw refusals and damage exist, but there is no episode report for repeated attempts, menu dwell by panel, navigation loops, stalled goals, near-empty air/power followed by recovery, or cue-to-damage timing. Do not call repeated positions “lost” without supporting behavior/notes. Purposeful returns are explicitly wanted in GAME-DIRECTION and OPENING-DESIGN.
- **Clarity:** threat emission is not proof that a warning was displayed, visible, heard, noticed or understood. Camera orientation, cue presentation, occlusion and panel context are incomplete. Canvas-only owner recordings make this especially important.
- **Hitches:** frame/component/GPU timings and nearby pictures are valuable. A large “outside” remainder or heap drop is a clue, not a proven browser/OS/GC cause. Event snapshots may arrive up to six frames after the triggering frame; video/telemetry clocks and missing-frame ranges matter.

### What the small sample established

1. `final/pack-4070-seg0`: **39 of 42 attention entries are long-frame groups**; it generates 43 strips including random controls. Its story is almost twice the 3090 story's length. Most rows are variations of “outside the game's frame.” Reading every strip would crowd out the two damage incidents and one milestone without establishing a 4070 performance verdict; this is a shared, indicative run. The traversal examples report **94–96% travelling** because that is their assigned task, so their activity share cannot diagnose campaign slog.
2. In `final/pack-3090-seg0`, A01 at 92.5 s shows a near-surface cockpit approach and slowdown. In the 4070 A16 strip at 147.2 s, the craft hits the visible shoreline and remains almost stationary. The one decoded driver frame at **about 149.6 s** makes **“Blocked ahead”** and **“[Hull impact]”** readable. The strip conveys motion; the larger frame answers the UI question. This is an observed scripted collision, not proof that an owner would become stuck or that the cue was noticed.
3. The 3090 R3 control strip at 74 s shows unflagged travel. The owner-export R1 strip at 11 s shows the cockpit **without HUD**, confirming the source-level capture limitation.
4. `views-3090-adverse2/.../cave.reef_archlet.interior.jpg` visibly distinguishes the deliberate lamp change. `views-3090-c/.../hub.crown_station.work.jpg` largely faces close geometry/water: a successful difference detector can still frame a weak quality-review question.

The old 4070 export similarly lacks three indexed pictures. This is concrete evidence for the later REC-1 export/integrity fixes, **not a claim that the current head still loses them**. Current code checks actual indexed files and export cutoff; the R2 handoff records newer successful exports. [R1, R3]

The seven opened files are the two damage strips above; `final/pack-3090-seg0/strips/R3-random-74s.jpg`; `final/playtest-3090-b/strips/R1-random-11s.jpg`; the two named fixed-view triptychs; and a frame decoded from `final/pack-4070-seg0/recording/video.webm`. ## Reading protocol and token budget

Follow [DIRECTION's tiered-evidence rule](../DIRECTION.md#evidence-reading-and-quality-review). Its roughly 6–10-strip budget is a ceiling for ordinary review, not a quota to fill. Escalate beyond it only for a named unresolved question; do not hide a blocking defect to meet a token target.

**Before opening a pack:** write at most three questions tied to the change and player intent. Examples: “Does the first lamp lead point somewhere useful?”, “Why did this return trip repeat?”, “Did the cave appear before the player arrived?” Owner notes choose the questions; technical alarms do not automatically outrank them. A crash/progress loss can still take precedence.

Choose one primary functional pack. For a matching second-machine run, read its summary and inspect differences/anomalies; repeat a visual pass only when a GPU/browser path changes the relevant behavior. Keep required two-machine evidence, without paying twice to interpret the same scene.

| Tier | Always/trigger | Reading and stopping rule | Planning cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0: eligibility | Always | Read summary once. Confirm source/build, human versus script, route/start state, run purpose, coverage/loss and performance qualification. Header/check lines only where summary lacks them. `partial` may simply mean short duration or shared performance. | Roughly 200–500 text tokens, including a small header extract. |
| 1: player story | Always for an experience review | Read story, owner notes and the short `analyseTimeline` report if supplied. Identify the top episodes, one successful outcome and missing evidence. Use **one** canonical progression analysis. On follow-up, read the affected delta and every earlier objection; do not re-ingest an unchanged story. | These stories ≈1.1–4.0k tokens at four characters/token; timeline/notes typically add a bounded 0.3–1k target, not measured here. |
| 2: visual test of a hypothesis | Notes, meaningful friction, changed visuals, adverse case, suspicious pacing/hitch | Usually 2–4 flagged sequences plus one unflagged control; up to 6–10 strips for broader risk. Include the relevant successful/adverse outcome. Open a readable frame when necessary. Stop when evidence supports a decision or clearly cannot answer it. | Text plus images. Reserve roughly 1–3k visual tokens per image as a loose planning allowance; actual model billing/resizing varies. Five images may add ≈5–15k. **Counting strips alone is insufficient.** |
| 3: diagnosis | One unresolved causal/temporal question | Query only that event/time interval in raw data; use short video or a narrow trace where needed. Produce one result in text, then stop. A human may use timeline.html; agents need not read its source. | Aim for ≤1–2k extracted text tokens per question plus 1–3 further images. Broader work needs an explicit question/budget. |
| 4: integration/taste | Once per milestone/wave, or a relevant regression | Existing composed check and assigned Opus taste/experience review. Use changed fixed views and a contact sheet to choose full frames. Coordinator consumes conclusions and inspects disputed/blocking evidence. | Separate wave budget; do not repeat it for each stream/reviewer. |

**Measured text sizes:** UTF-8 was read as text and characters counted; token values below are estimates at **4 characters/token**, not tokenizer/billing counts. Technical punctuation can materially raise token counts; allow roughly ±40%. No image-token measurement was available.

| Pack under `/work/tmp/rec1/` | Summary characters | Story characters | Estimated summary + story tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `final/playtest-3090-b` | 613 | 6,272 | 1,720 |
| `final/playtest-4070` | 614 | 4,402 | 1,250 |
| `final/pack-3090-seg0` | 579 | 8,307 | 2,220 |
| `final/pack-4070-seg0` | 621 | 15,944 | 4,140 |

All seven together are **59,062 characters, ≈14.8k text tokens before images**. In contrast, the two final driver packs contain about **2.2 and 2.6 MiB of raw NDJSON** each, potentially hundreds of thousands of text tokens. `try2/timeline.html` alone is about **14.2 MB**, largely embedded video. These are storage artifacts, not reading assignments. `analysis.json` is another 5–24 KB of largely duplicated facts.

### Sampling motion, long stretches and notes

- **Clarity/interaction:** start with 6–8 frames covering approach, cue, attempt, result and recovery, over roughly 8–15 seconds. Use 320–480-pixel scene tiles; use one 1280×720 frame or a UI crop for text. Do not enlarge 155-pixel tiles and infer unreadable words. Current prebuilt strips remain usable for motion; improved sparse layouts are a proposed change.
- **Collision, pop-in or control transition:** use the existing ±2-second/12-fps strip when ordering matters; then inspect 2–3 key frames at useful size. Retain fine telemetry; do not infer exact input latency or frame smoothness from this sampled video.
- **Pacing/“lost” notes:** inspect 6–12 frames distributed across 30–90 seconds before the note, with map/route and action context. If unresolved, examine one continuous 10–30-second sequence at the relevant turn. Four seconds centered on the note often shows the consequence after the cause has passed.
- **Hitch:** read frame timings and scope first. Inspect one before/during/after sequence if screen content matters. Repeated similar hitches need one representative and one contrasting case, with the full count retained in text.
- **Owner notes:** preserve the exact words and time/location. Join the prior lead, actions/refusals, vitals, panel/cue events and eventual outcome. Include positive notes and satisfying recoveries. A note is strongest evidence of that player's experience; it does not identify a technical cause by itself. No note means “unknown,” not “fine.” Ask a short retrospective question only where it would change the decision; do not interrupt every discovery to demand commentary.

The current `strip.mjs` can select ranges/rates, but its composer launches a browser. **Do not run it under a no-browser brief.** This report used existing strips and one offline decode. Future sparse sampling should have a CPU-only path or use the normal authorized recording workflow.

### Division of work and the output to keep

The **Opus builder** explains the intended player outcome, reads the relevant frames and records useful observations. The **fresh Sol reviewer** independently tests the highest-risk claims and all prior objections, using a small overlapping sample where independence matters; it need not duplicate every author image/check. The **coordinator** reads their conclusions, reconciles disputes and inspects material evidence on a flag. This follows the existing rule that builders/reviewers inspect frames and the coordinator consumes conclusions.

Keep one short finding list, normally 3–5 actionable items, without suppressing additional blockers. Each item needs: **scene/time → observed behavior → player consequence → severity/confidence → proposed root fix or next experiment → owner/check**. Mark **observed**, **inferred** or **human-test question**. Record compromises with root fix and cost, per DIRECTION. No second transcript of every check and image.

## Changes that would raise signal per token

Costs are relative engineering estimates, not commitments: **small** = a focused analysis/report change; **medium** = shared schema/integration plus focused checks; **large** = new runtime capture/control infrastructure. Keep one source of each fact. [R1–R5]

| Change | Value / cost | Owner and recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Put run purpose, human/script flag, starting capabilities, judged/disturbed status, loss/coverage and top three player episodes in summary | Very high / small | **REC-1 analysis follow-up.** Remove ambiguity without adding a certificate system. Include pre-window load errors: old `try1` has `errors: 0` in summary while the checks correctly fail errors during load. This is a summary usability gap, not a new crash finding. |
| Rank/group attention by impact and changed-system relevance; guarantee note/death/error coverage before a strip cap | Very high / small | **REC-1 pack fix.** Keep chronological timestamps/IDs, but make a ranked reading list. Collapse recurring same-context hitch/refusal/impact episodes. Retain totals and worst case; include one control. Do not generate only the first 40 chronological strips. |
| Join the existing timeline report into the pack once | Very high / medium | **REC-2 shared analysis**, with simulation/timeline owner. Export complete timeline metadata or normalize existing embedded events into the shared analyzer with honest missing boundaries. Add 1-minute bins of new things by kind, gaps, travel/idle and note markers; keep core progression on timeline play time and friction on wall time. **Do not create a third pacing classifier.** Wire the SIM-1 monotonic cursor seam when integrating REC-1 with the chunked root timeline. |
| Add friction episodes and time-to-first milestones from existing events/samples | High / small–medium | **REC-2.** First pass: refusals grouped by action/target/reason, repeated impacts + input + little movement, low-air/charge episodes, death→recovery, longest discovery/POI gaps. Suggest review thresholds, not automatic bad-design verdicts. Add menu open/close/panel identity only where missing; raw `active: false` cannot distinguish useful reading from confusion. |
| Carry semantic event IDs, outcome/reason, actor/target and clocks | High / medium | **REC-2 shared schema**, reusing sim events. Command type alone cannot reconstruct target or intent. Sparse outcome events are more useful than logging every movement command. Keep build/save/route IDs, units and schema version. |
| Sparse strips selected around notes/anomalies, with keyframe/full-resolution fallback | Very high / small–medium | **REC-1 analysis follow-up**, then **REC-2 CPU-only extraction**. Choose context length by question, not identical 48-frame sheets. Give missing/retired video ranges explicitly; fall back to the actual snapshot where available, including an export-tail note. |
| Record HUD/panel/cue presentation and identify capture coverage | Very high for clarity / medium; full-page owner capture large | **REC-2 with UI owner.** First label `canvasOnly`/`includesDOM`/`audio` in the pack, then sparse semantic UI/cue state and timestamps. Presentation telemetry still does not prove attention. Explore opt-in screen+audio capture only if the owner wants it; browser permissions and overhead make it unsuitable as the default solution. A desktop recording can answer a specific later audio/UI question. |
| Compare packs by semantic route milestones and matched capabilities | High / medium | **REC-2 extends existing `compare.mjs`**, rather than replacing it. It already aligns driver marks and compares technical numbers. Add new/resolved episodes and milestone/travel deltas; require comparable start save, route, craft, settings, recorder version and machine class. Label unmatched legs and disturbance. One owner on repeated builds is not an A/B population. |
| Repair fixed-view determinism and framing at the root | High / medium–large | **REC-1/CW-1/render owners**, selected in the once-per-wave taste/stewardship pass. Keep the 18 quarantined views out of passes; restore via deterministic readiness/fresh group loads. Version/reaccept useful station, landmark, cockpit and later time-of-day poses. Do not widen SSIM thresholds to conceal missing geometry. |
| Escalate selected hitch episodes to a bounded browser trace | High when unexplained / medium | **REC-2 reuses CW-1/profiling**, not always-on tracing. Correlate event/frame/GPU/GC tasks and page clock. Report p50/p95/p99, worst frame, counts and duration over 16.7/33/50/100 ms. Keep the owner's ~33 ms streaming rule; the other thresholds are diagnostics, not new acceptance gates. |
| One shared browser/driver library | High systemic value / medium | **Planned REC-2**, already assigned in STREAMS/CORE-HELPERS. Consolidate launch, clean start, save/input driver, clocks, recorder drain, metadata and result handling; parameterize scenario/policy. Delete replaced stream-driver forks in the same work. Avoid one new driver per metric. |

Minimum implementation should be report-only changes first. Instrument a missing field only when an actual question cannot be answered from current events, samples and notes. Preserve local-only storage and explicit loss reporting.

## Checks to drop or shrink

The process costs are observable; exact token savings and “findings per token” are not, because review token accounting is absent. Do not equate elapsed GPU minutes, test execution time and model tokens. A suite that runs with a compact result can be cheap in tokens but expensive in contention; a long report can be the reverse.

| Habit | Evidence and fair assessment | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every reviewer reruns the complete fast tier after a narrow fix | STEW-1 R4/R5/R6 reran **1,418 / 1,419 / 1,420 tests**, with test phases **442.1 / 357.5 / 439.9 s** under their one-CPU scopes: **20.7 minutes** combined. Their new findings concerned guard resolution/aliases, not reproduced gameplay regressions. R3 instead ran **15/15 focused guard/gate tests** and did not repeat the author's 1,415 tests. This is a useful internal example of focused review, not proof that full tests never help. [R6] | Retain author-required checks and **one canonical `npm run gate` at merge**. Reviewer runs the affected regressions/typechecks and audits the meaningful claims. Broaden only for a new failure, interface/composition change or unresolved risk. Do not invent a parallel hand-maintained gate. |
| New full review scope for each repair round | STREAMS records **11 TST-16 rounds**, **6 STEW-1 rounds**, **6 SIM-1 rounds before the split**, then **2 SIM-1a rounds**; REC-1 had at least **2** at this snapshot. Many late findings were real: admission/installer races and data-loss/protection bugs. SIM-1 R5 had six of nine findings in the note outbox; the later split removed substantial journal complexity from the immediate merge. [R5–R7] | Freeze the contract and unresolved-objection list. After two rounds exposing the same defect family, coordinator inspects the design/scope before commissioning another patch round. Consider removing duplication/state machines. This is a root-fix trigger, **not** a two-round acceptance limit or permission to waive real defects. |
| Treat guard review as an unbounded hostile-code proof | STEW-1 R5 found missing JSON/symlink gaps; coordinator then explicitly scoped it to a regression rail over honest code, with exotic bypasses out of scope unless ordinary code reaches them. [R5, R6] | Keep practical layering/reuse checks. Stop escalating speculative bypasses into indefinite release work after the agreed threat model is met. |
| Human/model reads every fixed view every round | 143 views captured in about **13 minutes on 3090 / 10 on 4070** in the handoff; 18 later quarantined. The R2 reviewer qualifies **125/125** as the remaining set's observed 3090 repeat, not independent determinism for every 4070 view. [R1, R3] | Read changed-view attention only; no tokens on 125 unchanged pictures. One taste pass per wave. Keep automatic baseline integrity checks and deliberate acceptance. The current capture cadence is owner policy; any move to affected subsets must be an explicit policy/configuration change, not a quiet shortcut. |
| Read all hitch strips, charts, analysis and raw rows | 4070 example: 39 hitch groups out of 42 attention entries, 43 generated strips; 15,944 story characters. The same facts recur in story, analysis, charts and timeline. | Read one representation first, group episodes and inspect representative/contrasting scenes. Never paste raw frames or timeline HTML by default. Do not call random-control sampling useless; it checks the detector's blind spot. |
| Repeated provenance/hash inventories and fresh captures solely for a documentation head | DIRECTION already rejects payload-hash inventories/re-attribution receipts. REC R2 explicitly distinguishes reusable unchanged fixed-view pictures from **nonreusable** evidence for changed export/clock/lifecycle behavior. [R3] | Keep one source SHA, relevant contracts and automatically checked baseline bytes. Reuse unaffected evidence with a precise limit; recapture changed behavior. Do not delete corruption detection because manual certificate writing is wasteful. |
| Repeat noisy performance A/B until the estimate looks good | REC-1 handoff reports four clean traveling off/playtest pairs: mean inclusive difference **0.30 ms/frame**, interval approximately **−0.13 to +0.73**. Self-time ≈0.09 ms does not settle inclusive cost. The R2 probe had divided callbacks rather than unique frames. STREAMS records local tests disturbing exclusive windows and forcing repeats. [R1, R3, R5] | Correct the denominator first; hold scene/settings/workload fixed; protect the exclusive window. Run the one bounded decisive check if acceptance still needs it, then report uncertainty. No timing loops over different scenes and no full suites alongside an exclusive run. |

**Expensive checks that earned their cost:** REC R1/R2 found false streaming passes, false-stable baselines, absent/late note pictures, quota/lifecycle defects, campaign-volume timeline failure, and segment-clock errors. The adverse lamp/camera controls demonstrated real visual detection; repeatability controls exposed history dependence. SIM-1's later findings could destroy/overwrite retained timelines; TST-16's could invalidate isolation or admission. Keep one focused long-volume/low-quota/restart control and relevant fault cases in their owning tests. The savings come from **reusing controls and narrowing follow-ups**, not replacing them with a happy-path screenshot. [R3, R7]

## What automated play can say about fun and pacing

Bots can demonstrate reachability, resource conservation, required recipe effort, repeated refusals/collisions, empty travel under a specified craft/loadout, mechanical recovery costs and the perfect-route floor of progression gaps. A wandering policy can expose alternative approaches the golden route omits. Both require declared controls and starting capabilities; an upgraded traversal save cannot establish first-expedition affordability or learnability.

Bots cannot establish tension, beauty, discovery satisfaction, understandable mystery, perceived fairness, auditory atmosphere, or whether a player wants another expedition. Raw novelty rate is not enjoyment: a strong vista can reward a quiet trip, while several automatic notices can add no meaningful discovery. Conversely, equal average rates can hide one long drought. Report semantic milestones and their sequence, not a scalar “fun score.”

Use the owner's **15–20-minute new-thing target**, **about 90 seconds between POIs**, **about five minutes per recipe-gathering trip**, **45–75-minute opening** and **10+ hour blind-play floor** as design questions with context. Count idle-only waiting separately; do not inflate duration with it. Menu/observation/route choice can matter to experience even when a progression clock omits them. A bot-to-human duration multiplier needs owner calibration by activity/leg, not one guessed universal factor. Repeated owner runs are increasingly knowledgeable and cannot recreate a fresh first-timer.

**Needed for a real experience verdict:** request a pack from the **next already-planned owner opening playtest**, preferably from New Game through the first expedition, with a few natural notes and the complete timeline export. Afterward ask: where did you want to go next; where did progress feel like work; which cue/choice was unclear; which moment made you want to continue? Keep substantial uninterrupted play. This report needs no fresh pack to recommend the process; the existing synthetic/traversal packs cannot supply that missing human judgment.

## External methods

These are practical adaptations, not additional acceptance requirements. I read online primary material, including Valve's full GDC slide text, EA SEED's paper implementation/results, vendor analytics/profiling guidance, and the authors' agent research. Sources and access limits follow. **Adopt** means useful now or in REC-2; **defer/skip** means the cost presently exceeds the likely decision value.

| Method and what it is | Fit for Siltwake | Cost/value and decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Structured observation / hypothesis-led tests:** observe behavior against a specific design question, distinguish action from interpretation. Valve treats designs as hypotheses and playtests as experiments. [E1] | Give each packet 2–3 questions; annotate “approached three hatches” separately from “did not understand the lead.” Include success as well as failure. | **Adopt now.** Almost no infrastructure; highest value per reading token. A generic 100-item audit is unnecessary. |
| **Think-aloud:** player describes intentions/thoughts while acting, without coaching. Valve also describes distraction and biased accounts as limitations. [E1, slides 18–20] | Optional brief use for a confusing menu/lead, or retrospective notes after a segment. Owner audio is currently absent; typed N notes work. Preserve uninterrupted exploration for atmosphere/timing. | **Adopt selectively.** Valuable intent; continuous narration of a ten-hour game burdens play and contaminates timing. Never demand it everywhere. |
| **RITE:** rapidly iterate and reevaluate a clearly diagnosed usability problem rather than wait for a large fixed study. [E2] | After one unambiguous blocker, fix the root cause and check the affected task at the next session. Version every packet. A replay by the informed owner checks the fix, not first-time discovery. | **Adopt the small iteration loop.** No population-level confidence or formal RITE-study claim from one owner. Full chapter inaccessible; no claimed case-study statistics. |
| **Games heuristic evaluation (PLAY):** experts use game-specific principles to locate likely usability/playability issues. [E3] | Once-per-wave Opus taste/experience pass can ask about readable goals/cues, feedback, control, challenge and unnecessary work, anchored to actual scenes and GAME-DIRECTION. | **Adopt a short lens.** Cheap hypothesis generation; no 116-item compliance spreadsheet or substitute for owner enjoyment. Published abstract supports the method; its full heuristic list was not read. |
| **Semantic event taxonomy:** typed events with defined parameters and validation. Vendor guidance uses event schemas and matching typed emitters. [E4] | Extend existing sim/timeline events with stable target/reason/outcome and clocks. Separate attempt, refusal, success, cue presentation and milestone. Preserve source/human/script labels. | **Adopt in REC-2.** Medium integration cost; improves every later analysis. **Skip** a new cloud SDK/dashboard for this local-only workflow. |
| **Funnels and time to first X:** follow eligible players/tasks through ordered or branching stages and measure time to completion. [E5] | One-session journey: cue available → inspected → recipe known → gather → craft → successful use. Opening threads are alternatives: represent branches, not one compulsory order. Start timing from actual opportunity; retain unfinished tasks as censored. | **Adopt a local journey table in REC-2.** Useful with one owner for locating friction, not conversion-rate inference. Counts require eligible opportunities, not all packets as a denominator. |
| **Heatmaps and death/fail maps:** locate clusters of behavior and failures. Valve shows death-concentration maps; EA shows exploration/terminal-state analysis. [E1, E6] | First list incidents by cave/site/craft/cause. When positions accumulate, draw separate depth/cave layers with dwell/exposure denominators. Overlay note/death/refusal points only for a named navigation question. | **Adopt the text clusters first; defer rich maps.** Raw death counts favor busy places; a top-down underwater heatmap merges vertically distinct routes. n=1 is not a population hotspot estimate. |
| **Session pacing curves:** preserve sequence and local gaps rather than average totals. Valve warns averages hide extremes; timeline already supplies semantics. [E1] | One-minute bins plus 5-minute trend for novelty, travel, waiting, recovery and notes; link the largest drought to its route and available options. Keep timers separate. | **Adopt in REC-2.** Cheap offline computation; one curve can replace many frame reads. Do not optimize for event spam. |
| **Churn/drop-off analysis:** study where people leave or fail to return. [E5's funnel approach] | Record end reason when volunteered: stopping for the evening differs from boredom, a crash or a script timeout. One solo owner cannot establish retention/churn rates. | **Skip population churn models/A/B statistics now.** A cheap stop-reason note is useful; a retention dashboard is not. |
| **Golden path plus bounded wandering:** completion tests and exploratory policies reveal different failures. EA's curiosity work rewards less-visited states and analyzes connectivity/traps. [E6, §§III–IV] | Keep both route completion bots. Add seeded wrong turns/alternate entrances/limited resources only around changed areas, with ordinary inputs and explicit coverage. Timeouts distinguish controller failure from an unreachable game state. | **Adopt small deterministic variants in REC-2.** Medium effort, high blind-spot value. EA's reported setup trained 320 agents: **skip RL training at our two-GPU scale** unless simpler policies fail on a real need. |
| **Coverage metrics:** measure states/transitions reached, not just a bot's finish flag. [E6] | Report eligible cave mouth→interior→exit transitions, route/craft/loadout/recovery cases and newly covered spatial cells. Exclude teleports from ordinary-travel claims; separate diagnostic loads. | **Adopt a compact coverage manifest.** Count uncovered cases, not screenshots. Crossing a cell says little about noticing a lead or enjoying it. |
| **Regression replays:** preserve a failing trajectory/start state and replay the affected behavior after a change; EA's stored trajectories support useful subsets. [E6] | Turn observed collisions, lost-note tails and recovery failures into short shared-driver scenarios. Store seed/save, actions/ticks, build and outcome; use semantic assertions/tolerances. | **Adopt in REC-2.** High reuse. Do not promise bit-exact browser/GPU replay; define what must reproduce. Do not add a mirrored test for every frame. |
| **LLM exploration/skill libraries:** Voyager uses curriculum, executable skills and environment feedback to explore Minecraft. [E7] | Borrow reusable action skills and diverse goals for the shared driver; require ordinary-control evidence for playable claims. Privileged state/API-driven skill execution is a different test class from visual discovery. | **Adopt the reusable-skill idea; defer live LLM control.** Token/time costs are high relative to a seeded driver; no evidence here validates an agent's “fun” judgment. |
| **Benchmark agent competence before interpreting failures:** BALROG evaluates game-playing LLM/VLM agents and reports long-horizon/vision weaknesses in tested models. [E8] | Use known-solvable tasks and controller success/failure reasons. Treat navigation loops as candidate game **or agent** problems. Current model skill must be measured; the paper's older model results are not estimates for today's Sol/Opus. | **Adopt the caution now.** Cheap. **Skip LLM-as-player-as-final-judge**: playing competence and human enjoyment prediction are different validations. |
| **Frame percentiles + incident traces:** inspect distributions/tails, presented/dropped frames and correlated CPU/GPU work rather than average FPS. Chrome documents frame categories and trace inspection. [E9] | Retain high-rate telemetry, summarize tails by scene, trace one unexplained episode. 3090 exclusive supplies target numbers; 4070 is a disturbed player-floor observation. Silent 12 fps video supplies context. | **Adopt selective escalation.** Bounded traces after a flag; **skip always-on deep stacks/screenshots and repeated hardware cross-products** without a changed risk. |
| **Severity × frequency × persistence, then practical priority:** Nielsen separates frequency, impact and whether a problem recurs; GUR SIG emphasizes fast actionable findings. [E10, E11] | Record impact, observed count/opportunities, confidence and persistence. Progress loss/crash or blocked play comes first; recurring confusion next; taste suggestions remain proposals. Coordinator sets priority using dependency/fix cost and owner goals. | **Adopt a small triage record.** Do not multiply made-up scores into false precision. Rare catastrophic loss can outrank frequent cosmetic noise. One root defect should produce one action, not twenty timestamp tickets. |

The external work changes three priorities: **protect uninterrupted human play**, **use semantic episodes and denominators rather than activity averages**, and **separate controller coverage from experience judgment**. None requires a new research bureaucracy.

External primary/practitioner sources, accessed during this research (no browser launches):

- **E1 — Mike Ambinder, Valve, GDC 2009, [Valve's Approach to Playtesting: The Application of Empiricism](https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/apps/valve/2009/GDC2009_ValvesApproachToPlaytesting.pdf).** Read slide text, especially 5, 13–26, 30–39 and 55–64. Direct studio basis for observation + verbal context + telemetry, limitations of averages, and avoiding costly over-analysis. Publisher's [index](https://www.valvesoftware.com/en/publications) verifies attribution.
- **E2 — Michael C. Medlock, [The Rapid Iterative Test and Evaluation Method (RITE)](https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198794844.003.0013), in *Games User Research* (2018).** Author/abstract verified through Crossref; full publisher chapter returned 403. Recommendation is an explicitly adapted rapid iteration loop; no original case-study results or formal study protocol are claimed.
- **E3 — Desurvire & Wiberg, [Game Usability Heuristics (PLAY) for Evaluating and Designing Better Games](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-02774-1_60), 2009.** Read published abstract (not full paywalled chapter). Supports using heuristics between empirical studies; does not warrant a universal enjoyment score.
- **E4 — Unity, [Create a custom event](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/analytics/events/custom-event).** Read schema/typed-event guidance. Adopt the data-design practice, not its service, parameter limits or SDK.
- **E5 — Unity, [Funnels tutorial](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/analytics/funnels/create-funnels).** Read step/completion/time analysis guidance. Adapt to local branching journeys; population monetization/retention examples do not fit n=1.
- **E6 — Gordillo, Bergdahl, Tollmar & Gisslén, EA SEED, [Improving Playtesting Coverage via Curiosity Driven Reinforcement Learning Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2103.13798), IEEE CoG 2021, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/CoG52621.2021.9619048).** Read implementation/results, especially count-based exploration, selective trajectory storage, connectivity and termination-state analysis. Provides concrete coverage ideas and illustrates why copying the full training infrastructure is excessive here.
- **E7 — Wang et al., [Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models](https://voyager.minedojo.org/), 2023.** Read authors' method/results overview. Evidence about exploration/skills in Minecraft, not enjoyment prediction or Siltwake visual-control competence.
- **E8 — Paglieri et al., [BALROG: Benchmarking Agentic LLM and VLM Reasoning On Games](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13543), ICLR 2025.** Read paper abstract and authors' benchmark overview. Grounds controller-competence caution; does not evaluate the current project's models or enjoyment judgments.
- **E9 — Chrome DevTools, [Performance features reference](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/performance/reference#frames).** Read frame categories, CPU/GPU inspection and capture options. Browser-native profiling semantics matter more here than adopting a different engine's profiler.
- **E10 — Jakob Nielsen, [Severity Ratings for Usability Problems](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/how-to-rate-the-severity-of-usability-problems/).** Read frequency/impact/persistence definitions and severity scale. Adapt judgment dimensions; do not map its numbers blindly onto repository P1/P2.
- **E11 — IGDA Games User Research SIG, [FAQs](https://www.gamesur.com/faqs/).** Read guidance on actionable insights, quick development cycles and practical evaluations. Supports concise evidence→action reporting.

GDC Vault redirected to maintenance, and Microsoft's TRUE paper landing page/ACM full text were inaccessible. Those are not evidence for additional claims here. Valve hosts its GDC material directly. Full-text access limits above are explicit; no secondary summary was silently substituted for an unread paper.

## Recommendation summary — one page for the owner

The recorder can make feedback much better if agents use it to explain a player's experience. More screenshots and repeated green tests do not automatically add understanding. The current packs are strongest at technical incidents; the next gain is connecting those incidents to what the player wanted to do.

### Do now

- Give each review **two or three player questions**. Read summary, story and your notes; inspect only the moments that can answer them, plus one ordinary moment the detector did not flag. The usual 6–10 strips are a budget, not a requirement to open ten.
- Let your notes lead. “I could not tell where to go” matters more for clarity than another identical hitch alert. Look back before the note to see the lead, attempt and result. Preserve good moments too.
- Use strips for movement and a larger frame for readable UI. Owner exports currently omit HUD/menus and sound, so agents must leave those judgments open when the evidence cannot show them.
- Keep one short list of observations, consequences and proposed actions. Separate what happened, what the agent suspects and what needs your play. Fix progress loss and repeated frustration first; avoid twenty tickets for one underlying problem.
- Keep the merge gate and meaningful independent review. Make follow-ups focus on changed risks and earlier objections. When repeated rounds expose the same design problem, simplify it before commissioning more patches.
- Use the next planned opening playtest for human pacing and enjoyment. Play mostly uninterrupted; a few natural notes and brief reflections afterward are enough. A bot cannot tell us whether a quiet swim felt atmospheric or empty.

### Do in REC-2

- Use **one shared driver and the existing play-timeline analyzer**. Add per-minute discovery/travel/waiting curves, time to first useful milestones and short friction episodes. Do not build another pacing system.
- Rank attention by player impact. Guarantee context for notes, deaths and failures; group repeated hitches. Generate a few larger, relevant frames instead of dozens of nearly identical tiny ones.
- Add sparse action targets/results and UI/cue presentation context. Label whether a recording includes HUD and audio. Compare builds only when route, starting tools, settings and hardware make the comparison meaningful.
- Keep both completion routes; add a few reproducible wandering/alternate-approach cases around changed areas. Report coverage and controller failures honestly. Borrow exploration ideas from research without training hundreds of agents.

### Stop doing

- Reading every unchanged fixed view, all raw telemetry, duplicated charts/JSON or entire video/HTML by default. Keep the once-per-wave taste review and investigate changed or quarantined views appropriately.
- Repeating broad reviewer suites and full evidence production after narrow fixes when they cannot answer a new question. Keep the canonical merge gate; reuse unaffected evidence with its actual source.
- Chasing noisy performance differences by repeating different routes, or calling recorder self-time its whole cost. Protect one controlled measurement when it is actually needed.
- Treating travel share, bot completion, event counts, a green pack, a heatmap or an LLM's opinion as a “fun score.” The owner judges feel; agents should make that judgment easier and turn it into clear, testable improvements.
